_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: issue #115 (reporter @AvlCompCo), fixed 2026-06-16. The fix is documentation + error-string only; no new flag/command. N-able removed the per-user 'API access' checkbox and moved to dedicated API Users; API Users still authenticate via the JSON-RPC Login method (partner=customer name, username=API-user login, password=API token -> visa), so COVE_PARTNER is REQUIRED for them. There is no bearer/header auth in the Cove API; the API token is the Login password, not a visa. Issue #133 (same reporter, on v0.1.2): clarified that COVE_PARTNER must be the FULL customer/partner string shown in the Cove console customer dropdown (usually including the account email in parentheses, e.g. 'Acme Corp (admin@acme.com)'), not just the company name -- Cove returns the same 2100 error for a wrong COVE_PARTNER format as for a bad password; and decoded the 13501 'Operation failed because of security reasons' visa error (the API User's role may not permit the method) while documenting that the raw generated endpoint commands need an explicit --visa "$(cove-cli auth token)" and that `cove-cli call <Method>` injects it automatically. Documentation + error-string only; no new flag/command.

handfixes.why: Cove's data-2100 'Unknown partner/username' is most often an empty COVE_PARTNER for an API User scoped to a customer. The original hint pointed at the removed per-user 'API access' checkbox, which no longer exists in backup.management. Re-derived from N-able's API User authorization docs (issue #115).

handfixes.summary: COVE_PARTNER documented as the full console-dropdown string (incl. account email); 13501 visa error decoded; raw-endpoint commands point to --visa / `cove-cli call`
handfixes.why: Issue #133 reporter set COVE_PARTNER to the bare company name and got the same 2100 error as a bad password; the working value is the full customer dropdown string including the email in parentheses. They also hit 13501 on the raw generated endpoint commands, which bypass the coverpc visa lifecycle (manual --visa). A reprint regenerates the auth help/docs and would drop both clarifications and the 13501 decode. Derived from issue #133 (reporter @AvlCompCo).

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For cove the manifest gained: COVE_BASE_URL, COVE_PARTNER, COVE_PASSWORD, COVE_USERNAME. server.json gained: COVE_BASE_URL, COVE_PARTNER, COVE_PASSWORD, COVE_USERNAME. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: COVE_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.
